diagnosis: Follicular thyroid adenoma with papillary architecture in a patient with Carney complex
legend: This tumour has intrafollicular centripetal papillary projections. Consistent with the morphological findings, the patient had a suppressed TSH level.

diagnosis: Carney complex–related pituitary neuroendocrine tumour (PitNET)/adenoma consisting of a mixed somatotroph and lactotroph tumour
legend: The tumour consists of a mixture of acidophilic (densely granulated somatotroph tumour) and chromophobic (sparsely granulated lactotroph) cells.

legend: ERα is positive in the lactotroph tumour component, whereas the somatotroph tumour cells are negative for ERα.

diagnosis: Growth hormone–producing adenoma in a patient with Carney complex
legend: MRI after gadolinium enhancement of the pituitary gland of a patient with Carney complex who had few obvious clinical signs of acromegaly. A developing microadenoma can be seen on the left side as a hypodense region with the gland. This is a common scenario among patients with the complex: biochemically, they meet all criteria of acromegaly, with elevated growth hormone levels and high IGF1. Yet in most patients, adenomas develop slowly within the background of hyperplasia. In this patient, who was followed for > 20 years, an obvious adenoma developed > 10 years after the first biochemical evidence of acromegaly.

title: Diagnostic criteria for Carney complex {11549623; 27943004}
tablehtml:
For a diagnosis of Carney complex, the patient must:

1. Exhibit two of the manifestations of the disease listed below

 

Spotty skin pigmentation with a typical distribution: lips, conjunctiva and inner or outer canthi, vaginal and penile mucosa

 

Myxomas, cutaneous and mucosal

 

Cardiac myxoma

 

Breast myxomatosis

 

Primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease

 

Acromegaly due to growth hormone–producing pituitary adenoma / pituitary neuroendocrine tumour (PitNET)

 

Large cell calcifying Sertoli cell tumour or characteristic calcification on testicular ultrasonography

 

Thyroid carcinoma or multiple hypoechoic nodules on thyroid ultrasonography

 

Psammomatous melanotic schwannoma

 

Blue naevus or epithelioid blue naevus, multiple

 

Breast ductal adenomas, multiple

 

Osteochondromyxoma of bone

2. OR exhibit one of the manifestations listed above and meet one of the supplemental criteria listed below

 

Affected first-degree relative

 

Inactivating mutation of PRKAR1A

Note: Carney complex is a rare disease, so population-based studies of this condition and incidences of specific manifestations are lacking in the world literature. Major centres for the disease, including the US National Institutes of Health (NIH), Mayo Clinic (USA), and Hôpital Cochin (France), have collated data on > 750 cases of the disease, including subsets that have been reported previously {11549623; 19293268}. The table reflects an adaptation of these data {26130139}.
